svg.title: Five questions walked in order, each with the answer that stops the walk, forming a Layer 2 design decision tree
svg.desc: A vertical chain of five numbered questions. The first asks whether the Layer 2 domain must span more than one access switch; no ends in a local VLAN on a single switch. The second asks whether Layer 2 is genuinely required; no ends in Layer 3 to the access layer. The third asks whether two uplinks can reach two independent devices; no means accepting single-homing in writing. The fourth asks whether those devices support clustering; no leads to an STP U-shape with the root on the gateway, yes leads to clustering where every uplink forwards but the peer link becomes the single point. The fifth asks whether any daisy chain or single-homed access switch remains; yes means fixing the orphan before tuning timers. An exit box lists what a finished design shows, and a closing note says the tree exists to make design arguments cheap.
svg.text: Five questions, in this order, decide almost every Layer 2 design
Walk from the top; the first question answered "no" usually ends the discussion
① Must this Layer 2 domain span
more than one access switch?
no
yes
No → one access switch, one local VLAN, stop here
A single switch cannot form a loop with itself, so STP becomes a formality and convergence is a link event.
② Is Layer 2 genuinely required
(one subnet, non-IP protocol,
VM migration, legacy system)?
no
yes
No → Layer 3 to the access layer
No loop exists, so nothing has to be blocked or tuned. The cheapest convergence is the one you never measure,
and the first hop stops being a shared resource two switches have to agree about.
③ Can the two uplinks reach two
independent devices?
no
yes
No → accept single-homing, in writing
One device, one feed, one rack. A redundant drawing does not create redundant power; record the exposure.
④ Do those two devices support
clustering (vPC, VSS, stacking
or standard M-LAG)?
choose
either way
No → STP U-shape: VLANs stay local, uplinks paired, root on the gateway switch
Yes → clustering: every uplink forwards, but the peer link becomes the new single point
Either answer is defensible; only the failure you cannot name is not. Both need root and gateway aligned.
⑤ Any daisy chain or single-homed
access switch left?
yes
no
Yes → fix the orphan before tuning a single timer
It is the failure domain you did not choose. Three chained switches are three reboots of exposure.
A finished design shows four things: every uplink either forwards or is documented as blocked, one switch holds root and gateway per VLAN,
the physical independence of any two "redundant" paths is drawn, and the convergence budget is written end to end rather than per protocol.
The tree exists to make arguments cheap: two questions about scope decide whether Layer 2 should span, two about physical independence decide the mechanism.
Once those four answers are on the whiteboard, the vendor choice is a procurement detail, not a design debate. What remains is configuration and proof.
